newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel breaks 3.5 to the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel breaks 3.5 to the dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel on Tuesday declined for the third consecutive session against the dollar and the basket of foreign currencies in very volatile trading, dealers said.
On Monday the shekel dropped 1.4 percent, following a 0.5 percent decline on Friday.

"Trading was very volatile today and the market suffered wild swings," said a dealer at the First International Bank of Israel (FIBI). He said that during early trading the shekel fell from 3.5 shekels per dollar to 3.6 shekels.
"When the dollar reached 3.6 investors came in, pushing the shekel upwards," he said. In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5050 shekels.
"It's the plan, it's politics, it's interest rates, it's the press. The market is nervous," said Ilan Viskin of Bank Hapoalim.

Last week the central bank lowered its key lending rate 1.2 percentage points to an annual 12.7 percent and the cabinet approved exchange rate reform which widened the upper limit of the shekel's trading band. This increased the risk of a depreciation of the shekel, which had been trading at the bottom limit for much of the past year.
Dealers said the market was also affected by options dealers who tried to keep the dollar at 3.5 shekels ahead of the expiry of the Maof dollar options for June on Tuesday.

"This is not a new trend. Some investors panicked because of the political and economic uncertainty and started buying dollars. I believe that in a week or two the shekel will start rising again," the FIBI dealer said.
Dealers have said the private sector, faced with growing uncertainty, preferred to pay off foreign currency loans now.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5060 shekels against 3.4840 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.8142 against 3.7869 on Monday.
The shekel also traded against the yen at 3.0580 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.0188 on Monday, and against the mark at 2.0326 shekels compared with 2.0197 on Monday.
